instructions: This is a webcam-controlled 3D basketball game built with React Three Fiber, TypeScript strict mode, and MediaPipe hand tracking. Review every file thoroughly. Flag ALL issues you find — we want zero remaining problems. Focus especially on: runtime bugs, state management issues, memory leaks, animation/physics correctness, React hook dependency arrays, Three.js resource disposal, and TypeScript strictness violations.

rules.rule: Do not use singleton pattern for game engine classes. This project uses React hooks + state + R3F useFrame for the game loop, not singleton orchestrators.
Do not import or reference pixi.js or any 2D rendering. This project is 3D-only using React Three Fiber.
All Three.js geometries, materials, and textures must be disposed on component unmount to prevent memory leaks.
Do not allocate new THREE.Vector3, THREE.Quaternion, or other objects inside useFrame or render loops. Pre-allocate as refs.
All useEffect, useCallback, and useMemo dependency arrays must include all referenced values. Use refs to break unnecessary re-subscriptions for values that change frequently.
Shot detection must require BOTH hand above shoulder (position gate) AND wrist flick (velocity gate). Single-condition triggers are bugs.
Do not use @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, or 'as any' type casts. Fix the types properly.
All animations and physics must use deltaTime, not frame count. Values like 'smoothing *= 0.9' per frame are frame-rate dependent bugs.
